cards.explanation: The answer is Pharaoh's palace. Joseph collects all the money in Egypt and Canaan, and "…he brought it into Pharaoh’s palace." (Genesis 47:14) Joseph, Jacob's son, isn't pocketing a coin of it. That's a LOT of money going through one door, friends.

The answer is False. Joseph says, "Then bring me your livestock… I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock." (Genesis 47:16) The money ran out, but the selling didn't stop. The payment just changed to horses, flocks, herds and donkeys (Genesis 47:17).

The answer is their bodies and their land. In the second year they tell Joseph, "There is nothing left for our lord except our bodies and our land." (Genesis 47:18) Money gone, livestock gone, and that's the list. I think that has to be a hard thing to say out loud.

The answer is slaves to Pharaoh. The Egyptians say, "Then we, along with our land, will be slaves to Pharaoh." (Genesis 47:19) It's their own offer, and they make it so they won't perish. I think this one is heavy, friends.

The answer is True. The Egyptians ask, "Give us seed that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate." (Genesis 47:19) Food gets them through today. Seed is what gets them a harvest later. They're asking for both.

The answer is the priests. The text says Joseph "…did not acquire the priests’ portion of the land…" (Genesis 47:22) Everybody else's fields went to Pharaoh. The priests walked away still holding theirs.

The answer is True. Pharaoh was already supplying the priests, and the text ties that straight to their land. It says their land "…had been given to them by Pharaoh. They ate the rations that Pharaoh supplied; so they did not sell their land." (Genesis 47:22) Everybody else showed up with empty pockets, and the priests were already covered. The reason is sitting right there in the verse, friends.

The answer is that the people keep it. Joseph says, "…four-fifths will be yours as seed for the field and food for yourselves and your households and children." (Genesis 47:24) One fifth to Pharaoh, four fifths for the people's own fields and tables. That's a lot of the batch staying in their kitchen.

The answer is that he has saved their lives. "You have saved our lives…" the people tell Joseph. "We have found favor in our lord’s eyes, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants." (Genesis 47:25) Joseph had just handed them seed and told them about the harvest, and that's their answer.

The answer is False, friends! Joseph "…established a law that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh, and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day." (Genesis 47:26) Nothing in that verse ties the law to the famine ending. That's a law with staying power, like a subscription you forgot to cancel. And the verse adds one more thing: only the priests' land does not belong to Pharaoh.
